name: NOMINAL
description: NOMINAL returns the nominal annual rate given the effective annual rate and the number of compounding periods per year.
tldr: Calculates the nominal annual interest rate from an effective rate.

parameters.name: npery
parameters.description: Number of compounding periods per year.

basicExample.description: Nominal rate from an effective annual rate
basicExample.explanation: An effective annual rate of 6.17% with monthly compounding corresponds to a 6% nominal rate.

advancedExamples.title: Annual percentage rate calculation
advancedExamples.description: Find the nominal APR from an effective rate
advancedExamples.explanation: An 8% effective annual rate with monthly compounding corresponds to a 7.72% nominal rate.

howItWorks: NOMINAL is the inverse of EFFECT. It computes the nominal rate that, when compounded npery times per year, produces the given effective annual rate.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Result is the nominal annual rate, not the periodic rate.

commonErrors.cause: npery is less than 1 or effect_rate is invalid.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure npery >= 1 and effect_rate is a positive decimal.

commonErrors.cause: Effective rate was entered as a percentage instead of a decimal.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: NOMINAL works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between NOMINAL and EFFECT?
faq.answer: NOMINAL converts effective to nominal. EFFECT converts nominal to effective.

faq.question: When do I need NOMINAL?
faq.answer: When you know the effective annual rate and want to express it as a nominal annual rate for disclosure or comparison.
